entries.claim: For every fixed join query Q, Theorem 11 gives O(N^(1+mw(Q))) preprocessing, O(N^mw(Q)) amortized single-tuple insert/delete update time including major and minor rebalancing, and O(1) output enumeration delay.
limitations: Query fixed; theorem's direct scope is join/full CQ.
No separate peak-space theorem for all materialized state stated in Theorem 11.
Published ACM text was not compared to arXiv version line-by-line.

entries.claim: The method already reacts to heavy/light membership changes with minor rebalancing and to database-size changes with major rebalancing; relaxed boundaries (approximately 1/2 and 3/2 M^epsilon) prevent one-update threshold oscillation, and both costs amortize into O(N^mw) per update.
limitations: The exponent epsilon remains fixed after query-level maintenance-width optimization.
This is not per-instance online epsilon selection.

entries.claim: A data-dependent online epsilon policy is formally distinct from fixed query-optimal epsilon, but no precise causal benchmark, migration-correct algorithm, or improvement theorem was established in this cycle.
limitations: This is not a proof that all online adaptive IVM is solved.
No algorithm-design task or successor is created.

entries.claim: A rebuild-on-every-switch threshold portfolio can incur a rebuild-scale cost on every alternating regime; this rejects the naïve switch implementation only, not all incremental migration designs.
limitations: No implementation or experiment was run.
A more sophisticated exact migration may avoid full rebuild; its bound remains open.
